title: Reinforcement Learning Pair Trading: A Dynamic Scaling approach

extraction.methodology_summary: The paper constructs reinforcement learning (RL) environments for pair trading cryptocurrencies, combining cointegration-based spread calculation with dynamic action spaces. Pairs are selected via Pearson correlation and Engle-Granger cointegration tests on 1-minute interval data. Grid search is utilized to find optimal parameters (window size, open/close thresholds), and actor-critic algorithms (primarily A2C) are trained to determine trade timing (RL1) or both timing and dynamic investment quantities (RL2).
extraction.universe: Binance cryptocurrency market (specifically BTC-GBP and BTC-EUR pairs)

performance_metrics.context: Gatev et al. (2006) traditional pair trading strategy
Gatev et al. (2006) traditional pair trading strategy

key_findings: Reinforcement learning significantly outperforms traditional rule-based pair trading techniques when applied to volatile cryptocurrency markets.
Allowing the RL agent to dynamically scale investment quantities (RL2) leads to substantially higher profits compared to binary timing-only decisions (RL1).
A2C outperformed other algorithms such as PPO, DQN, and SAC in the pair trading environment.
Transaction costs heavily impact high-frequency crypto trading profitability, though RL models maintain outperformance at lower fee tiers.
limitations: Relatively limited dataset scope restricted to specific crypto pairs and a short timeframe.
Focusing only on two-leg strategies restricts complex arbitrage opportunities.
High computational demand and resource intensity during training.
Model lacks consideration for certain real-world friction factors.
